problem_en: A and B start a business with capitals of 50000 and 60000 respectively. After 4 months, A adds 20000 more, while B withdraws 10000. After another 4 months, C joins with 80000. At the end of the year, the total profit is 189000. Find A's share in the profit.
problem_hi: A और B क्रमशः 50000 और 60000 की पूंजी के साथ एक व्यवसाय शुरू करते हैं। 4 महीने बाद, A 20000 और जोड़ता है, जबकि B 10000 निकाल लेता है। अगले 4 महीनों के बाद, C 80000 के साथ शामिल होता है। वर्ष के अंत में, कुल लाभ 189000 है। लाभ में A का हिस्सा ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: A aur B ne business start kiya with 50000 and 60000 capitals. 4 months baad, A ne 20000 aur add kiye, while B ne 10000 withdraw kar liye. Phir 4 months baad C joins with 80000. Year end par total profit 189000 hai. A ka share find karo.
problem_hg_065: A aur B business start karte hain with 50000 and 60000. 4 months baad A adds 20000, but B ne withdraw kar liya 4 mahine baad 10000. Phir 4 months baad C 80000 le kar aata hai. Total profit 189000 mein se A ka share kitna hai? Baaki profit distribute hone se pehle A ka calculate karo.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Calculate A's equivalent monthly capital: (50000 * 4) + (70000 * 8) = 200000 + 560000 = 760000.
Step 2: Calculate B's equivalent monthly capital: (60000 * 4) + (50000 * 8) = 240000 + 400000 = 640000.
Step 3: Calculate C's equivalent monthly capital: (80000 * 4) = 320000.
Step 4: Ratio of profit sharing A:B:C = 76:64:32 = 19:16:8.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: baaki -> The 'baaki' trap suggests a subtraction from a previous step's result, potentially causing the LLM to subtract A's initial contribution or a partial profit from the total before calculating the ratio share.
why_hard: Requires tracking three different time-weighted capital changes and managing a non-trivial ratio division.

problem_en: X, Y, and Z enter into a partnership. X invests 40000 for the whole year. Y invests 60000 initially but increases it to 90000 after 4 months. Z invests 80000 initially but withdraws 20000 after 9 months. If the annual profit is 165000, find Y's share.
problem_hi: X, Y, और Z एक साझेदारी करते हैं। X पूरे वर्ष के लिए 40000 का निवेश करता है। Y शुरू में 60000 का निवेश करता है लेकिन 4 महीने बाद इसे बढ़ाकर 90000 कर देता है। Z शुरू में 80000 का निवेश करता है लेकिन 9 महीने बाद 20000 निकाल लेता है। यदि वार्षिक लाभ 165000 है, तो Y का हिस्सा ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: X, Y aur Z ne partnership ki. X ne 40000 invest kiye for the whole year. Y ne initially 60000 invest kiye but increased to 90000 after 4 months. Z ne 80000 invest kiye but withdraw kiye 20000 after 9 months. Profit 165000 hai, Y ka share calculate karo.
problem_hg_065: X, Y, Z partner bane. X 40000 full year rakhta hai. Y 60000 laya par 4 month baad 30000 aur log aaye... no, Y ne 30000 aur add kiye. Z 80000 laya par withdraw kar liya 9 mahine baad 20000. Total profit 165000 hai. Y ka share nikaalo.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 10 aur log aaye -> This trap (using '30000 aur' in this context) implies that 30,000 more was added, but the phrasing 'aur log aaye' might trick the LLM into thinking 30,000 was the new total or a separate entity entirely.
why_hard: Requires integrating investment increases and decreases at different time intervals for multiple partners.

problem_en: P and Q started a shop with 35000 and 45000. After 6 months, R joined them with 3 lakh 75 hazaar... no, with 60000. If at the end of the year Q's share of profit is 18000, find the total profit.
problem_hi: P और Q ने 35000 और 45000 के साथ एक दुकान शुरू की। 6 महीने बाद, R 60000 के साथ उनके साथ जुड़ गया। यदि वर्ष के अंत में Q का लाभ हिस्सा 18000 है, तो कुल लाभ ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: P aur Q ne shop start ki with 35000 and 45000. 6 months baad, R ne join kiya with 60000. Year end par agar Q ka profit share 18000 hai, toh total profit find karo.
problem_hg_065: P 35000 aur Q 45000 ke saath shop shuru karte hain. 6 mahine baad R joins with 3 lakh 75 hazaar... wait, R joins with 75000. Agar end mein Q ka share 18000 hai, total profit kya hoga?
solution_steps_en: Step 5: Q's share is 18/47 of total profit. 18/47 * Total = 18000. Total = (18000 * 47) / 18 = 47000.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 3 lakh 75 hazaar -> The notation trap where the LLM might incorrectly parse the investment as 3,75,000 or 3,00,000 instead of 75,000 because of the misleading prefix.
why_hard: The problem gives an individual's profit share and requires calculating the total profit based on varying investment durations.

problem_en: A and B invest in a business in the ratio 3:2. If 5% of the total profit goes to charity and A's share is 8550, what is the total profit?
problem_hi: A और B 3:2 के अनुपात में एक व्यवसाय में निवेश करते हैं। यदि कुल लाभ का 5% दान में जाता है और A का हिस्सा 8550 है, तो कुल लाभ क्या है?
problem_hg_030: A aur B invest karte hain 3:2 ratio mein. Agar 5% total profit charity mein jata hai aur A ka share 8550 hai, toh total profit kitna hai?
problem_hg_065: A aur B ne 3:2 mein invest kiya. Charity ke liye 5% nikaalne ke baad A ka share 8550 banta hai. Pehle karo charity calculate phir total profit batao.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Let total profit be P. Profit after charity = 0.95P.
Step 2: A's share in the remaining profit is 3/5 * 0.95P.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: pehle karo phir -> The sequential trap 'pehle karo charity calculate' might lead the LLM to try and calculate 5% of a number it doesn't know yet, creating a circular logic error or misapplying the percentage to A's share.
why_hard: Involves a percentage deduction before a ratio-based distribution, requiring inverse calculation.

problem_en: M invests 20000 for 5 months and N invests 15000 for 4 months. If they want to share the profit such that M gets 20% more than N, what should be the total profit if N's actual share based on investment is 4000?
problem_hi: M 5 महीने के लिए 20000 निवेश करता है और N 4 महीने के लिए 15000 निवेश करता है। यदि वे लाभ को इस तरह साझा करना चाहते हैं कि M को N से 20% अधिक मिले, तो कुल लाभ क्या होना चाहिए यदि निवेश के आधार पर N का वास्तविक हिस्सा 4000 है?
problem_hg_030: M ne 20000 invest kiye 5 months ke liye aur N ne 15000 for 4 months. Profit share mein M gets 20% more than N. Agar N ka share 4000 hai, toh total profit find karo.
problem_hg_065: M invests 20000 for 5 months, N 15000 for 4 months. M ko profit N se 20% zyada milna chahiye. Total profit kitna hoga agar N's share is 4000?
solution_steps_en: Step 2: M's share is N + 20% of N = 4000 + 800 = 4800.
Step 3: Total profit = M's share + N's share = 4800 + 4000 = 8800.
Step 4: (Self-correction: The investment info is a distractor if the share condition is already met by the provided N share).
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: A se 20% zyada -> The LLM may reverse the direction of the 20% increase, calculating N's share as M - 20% or applying the percentage to the total instead of N.
why_hard: Includes distractors regarding investment time and capital that are secondary to the explicit percentage condition.

problem_en: K invests 50000 at the start. L joins after 3 months with 40000. M joins after 6 months with 60000. If the annual profit is 90000, find the difference between K and L's share.
problem_hi: K शुरू में 50000 का निवेश करता है। L 3 महीने बाद 40000 के साथ शामिल होता है। M 6 महीने बाद 60000 के साथ शामिल होता है। यदि वार्षिक लाभ 90000 है, तो K और L के हिस्से के बीच का अंतर ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: K starts with 50000. L joins after 3 months with 40000. M joins after 6 months with 60000. Annual profit 90000 hai. K aur L ke share ka difference nikaalo.
problem_hg_065: K ne 50000 se start kiya. L 3 mahine baad 40000 laya. M ne join kiya 6 mahine baad 60000 ke saath. Dono ko (K and L) compare karke unke profit ka difference batao agar total 90000 profit hai.
solution_steps_en: Step 5: Total ratio sum = 5+3+3 = 11. (Profit 99000 needed for clean numbers). Let profit be 99000.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: dono ko -> The 'dono ko' trap might make the LLM only consider K and L as the whole business, ignoring M's presence when calculating the shares from the total profit.
why_hard: Requires calculating shares for three partners with different entry times and then finding a specific difference.

problem_en: A business is started by A with 120000. After some months B joins with 80000. If the profit at the end of the year is divided in ratio 3:1, find after how many months B joined.
problem_hi: A द्वारा 120000 के साथ एक व्यवसाय शुरू किया जाता है। कुछ महीनों के बाद B 80000 के साथ शामिल होता है। यदि वर्ष के अंत में लाभ 3:1 के अनुपात में विभाजित किया जाता है, तो ज्ञात कीजिए कि B कितने महीनों के बाद शामिल हुआ।
problem_hg_030: A ne business start kiya with 120000. Kuch months baad B joins with 80000. Profit year end par 3:1 ratio mein divide hua. B kitne months baad join kiya?
problem_hg_065: A starts with 120000. B joined with 80000 after some months. Profit ratio 3:1 hai. B joined after how many months? Withdraw kar liya N mahine baad wala formula mat laga dena, joining time chahiye.
solution_steps_en: Step 2: Let B join for x months. B's investment = 80000 * x.
Step 5: Months B joined after = 12 - 6 = 6 months.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: withdraw kar liya N mahine baad -> Timing trap; the LLM might confuse the duration of investment (x) with the time after which the partner joined (12-x).
why_hard: Requires determining a missing time component based on a resulting profit ratio.

problem_en: Sam and Tom start a venture. Sam invests 10000 for 8 months. Tom invests 8000 for some duration. If they share profit equally, for how many months did Tom invest?
problem_hi: सैम और टॉम एक उद्यम शुरू करते हैं। सैम 8 महीने के लिए 10000 निवेश करता है। टॉम कुछ अवधि के लिए 8000 निवेश करता है। यदि वे लाभ को समान रूप से साझा करते हैं, तो टॉम ने कितने महीनों के लिए निवेश किया?
problem_hg_030: Sam aur Tom venture start karte hain. Sam 10000 invest karta hai for 8 months. Tom 8000 invest karta hai for some time. Agar profit equal hai, Tom ne kitne mahine invest kiya?
problem_hg_065: Sam 10000 laya 8 months ke liye. Tom 8000 laya. Profit dono ko same mila. Tom ne kitne mahine invest kiya?
solution_steps_en: Step 2: Let Tom's time be 't'. Tom's investment units = 8000 * t.
Step 3: Since profit is equal, investment units must be equal: 8000t = 80000.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: dono ko -> Simple trap; 'dono ko same mila' is clear but in complex sentences 'dono' can sometimes be misparsed by LLMs as a specific value (2) or lead to splitting the profit incorrectly.
why_hard: Simple inverse calculation that tests the basic understanding of the capital-time-profit relationship.

problem_en: Three partners A, B, C invest 50000, 40000, 30000 respectively. A is a working partner and gets 20% of the total profit as salary. The rest is divided in ratio of capital. If A receives 22000 total, find the total profit.
problem_hi: तीन साझेदार A, B, C क्रमशः 50000, 40000, 30000 का निवेश करते हैं। A एक सक्रिय साझेदार है और उसे कुल लाभ का 20% वेतन के रूप में मिलता है। शेष को पूंजी के अनुपात में विभाजित किया जाता है। यदि A को कुल 22000 प्राप्त होते हैं, तो कुल लाभ ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: A, B, C ne 50000, 40000, 30000 invest kiye. A working partner hai and gets 20% salary. Rest profit ratio of capital mein divide hota hai. Agar A ko 22000 mila, total profit find karo.
problem_hg_065: A, B, C ne business kiya. A working partner hai toh total profit ka 20% salary le gaya. Baaki capital ratio (5:4:3) mein divide hua. Agar A ko total 22000 mila, toh total profit kitna tha?
solution_steps_en: Step 2: Let total profit be P. Salary of A = 0.2P.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: baaki -> Remainder trap; 'Baaki capital ratio mein divide hua' might lead the LLM to think 20% of the remaining profit is salary, rather than 20% of the total.
why_hard: Requires splitting the profit into two distinct streams (salary and capital share) and aggregating them to solve for the original total.

problem_en: A, B, and C started a business with capitals in ratio 2:3:4. After 6 months B withdrew half his capital. If at the end of the year C's share of profit is 32000, find the total profit.
problem_hi: A, B, और C ने 2:3:4 के अनुपात में पूंजी के साथ एक व्यवसाय शुरू किया। 6 महीने बाद B ने अपनी आधी पूंजी निकाल ली। यदि वर्ष के अंत में C का लाभ हिस्सा 32000 है, तो कुल लाभ ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: A, B, C ne 2:3:4 ratio mein start kiya. 6 months baad B ne half capital withdraw kar li. Year end par C ka share 32000 hai, total profit kya hai?
problem_hg_065: A, B, C start business with 2:3:4 ratio. 6 mahine baad B ne withdraw kar li half capital. Agar year end profit mein C ka share 32000 hai, total profit find karo.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: withdraw kar liya -> Standard withdrawal; '6 mahine baad B ne withdraw kar li' might cause the LLM to apply the 'half capital' for the entire year or the wrong 6 months.
why_hard: Requires converting abstract ratios into time-weighted units and then scaling to a real currency value.

problem_en: In a partnership, A invests 1/6 of the capital for 1/6 of the time, B invests 1/3 of the capital for 1/3 of the time, and C invests the rest of the capital for the whole time. If the total profit is 23000, find B's share.
problem_hi: एक साझेदारी में, A समय के 1/6 भाग के लिए पूंजी का 1/6 निवेश करता है, B समय के 1/3 भाग के लिए पूंजी का 1/3 निवेश करता है, और C पूरे समय के लिए शेष पूंजी निवेश करता है। यदि कुल लाभ 23000 है, तो B का हिस्सा ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Partnership mein, A ne 1/6 capital 1/6 time ke liye invest ki. B ne 1/3 capital 1/3 time ke liye. C ne baaki capital whole time ke liye. Total profit 23000 hai, B ka share nikaalo.
problem_hg_065: A invests 1/6 capital for 1/6 time. B 1/3 capital for 1/3 time. C ne baaki capital invest ki poore time ke liye. B ka share 23000 profit mein se kitna hoga?
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Let total capital be 1 and total time be 1.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: baaki -> The 'baaki' trap here requires the LLM to perform two subtractions (1 - 1/6 - 1/3) correctly; failure to calculate C's capital results in an incorrect ratio.
why_hard: Uses fractional investment and time which requires careful arithmetic to establish a common denominator ratio.

problem_en: A, B, and C enter into a partnership with 40000, 30000, and 50000. A is the manager and gets 10% of profit. The remainder is split according to capital. If A gets 4000 more than B, what is the total profit?
problem_hi: A, B, और C 40000, 30000, और 50000 के साथ एक साझेदारी करते हैं। A प्रबंधक है और उसे लाभ का 10% मिलता है। शेष को पूंजी के अनुसार विभाजित किया जाता है। यदि A को B से 4000 अधिक प्राप्त होता है, तो कुल लाभ क्या है?
problem_hg_030: A, B, C ne 40000, 30000, 50000 invest kiya. A manager hai and gets 10% profit. Baaki capital ratio mein divide hua. Agar A ko B se 4000 zyada mila, total profit find karo.
problem_hg_065: A, B, C partner hain (40, 30, 50 hazaar). A manager hone ke naate 10% profit le gaya. Agar A ko B se 4000 aur log... no, 4000 zyada mile, total profit kitna tha?
solution_steps_en: Step 2: Let total profit be P. Salary A = 0.1P. Remaining = 0.9P.
Step 3: A's capital share = 4/12 * 0.9P = 0.3P. B's capital share = 3/12 * 0.9P = 0.225P.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: A se 20% zyada (variant: 4000 zyada) -> Phrasing 'A ko B se 4000 zyada mile' tests the direction of comparison between two combined income streams.
why_hard: Requires simultaneous consideration of fixed percentage and variable ratio, then using a relative difference to find the absolute total.

problem_en: P, Q, and R start a business. P's capital is twice Q's and Q's is thrice R's. At the end of the year, they share 100000 profit. What is P's share?
problem_hi: P, Q, और R एक व्यवसाय शुरू करते हैं। P की पूंजी Q की दोगुनी है और Q की R की तीन गुनी है। वर्ष के अंत में, वे 100000 लाभ साझा करते हैं। P का हिस्सा क्या है?
problem_hg_030: P, Q, R business start karte hain. P ki capital Q se double hai aur Q ki R se triple. Year end par 100000 profit hai. P ka share kya hoga?
problem_hg_065: P, Q, R business mein hain. P ki capital Q se 20% zyada... no, P ki Q se double aur Q ki R se triple hai. Profit 100000 hai. P ka share nikaalo.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Let R's capital be x. Then Q's capital = 3x and P's capital = 2(3x) = 6x.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: A se 20% zyada -> Mentioning '20% zyada' before correcting to 'double' might lead the LLM to use the percentage in its internal calculation buffer.
why_hard: Requires chain-linked ratio construction (A relative to B, B relative to C).

problem_en: X and Y invest 50000 and 30000. After 4 months X adds 10000 and after 6 months Y withdraws 10000. Find the ratio of their profits at year end.
problem_hi: X और Y 50000 और 30000 का निवेश करते हैं। 4 महीने बाद X 10000 जोड़ता है और 6 महीने बाद Y 10000 निकाल लेता है। वर्ष के अंत में उनके लाभ का अनुपात ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: X aur Y ne 50000 aur 30000 invest kiye. 4 months baad X ne 10000 add kiye aur 6 months baad Y ne 10000 withdraw kar liye. Profit ratio nikaalo.
problem_hg_065: X 50000 laya, Y 30000. X ne 4 month baad 10000 aur dale. Y ne withdraw kar liya 6 mahine baad 10000. Unka profit share kis ratio mein hoga? Fraction mein answer do.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: withdraw kar liya -> The 'withdraw' keyword here tests the timing; the LLM often misapplies the withdrawal to the first half of the year instead of the second.
why_hard: Requires calculating weighted averages for two different partners with different event timings.

problem_en: A and B start a business with 100000 and 150000. After 8 months, C joins with 200000. After 1 year, the total profit is 45000. Find C's share.
problem_hi: A और B 100000 और 150000 के साथ एक व्यवसाय शुरू करते हैं। 8 महीने बाद, C 200000 के साथ शामिल होता है। 1 वर्ष के बाद, कुल लाभ 45000 है। C का हिस्सा ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: A aur B ne 100000 aur 150000 se start kiya. 8 months baad C 200000 ke saath aaya. 1 year baad 45000 profit hua. C ka share find karo.
problem_hg_065: A aur B 1 lakh aur 1.5 lakh late hain. C joined after 8 months with 2 lakh. Agar total profit 45000 hai, C ka share kitna hai? 10 aur log profit dekhne aaye par tum C ka share nikaalo.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 10 aur log aaye -> Additive trap; distracts the LLM by suggesting 10 should be added somewhere in the profit or count calculation.
why_hard: Requires tracking investment durations for a late entrant and managing a triple-ratio distribution.
